movie.title: Until Dawn
movie.overview: One year after her sister Melanie mysteriously disappeared, Clover and her friends head into the remote valley where she vanished in search of answers. Exploring an abandoned visitor center, they find themselves stalked by a masked killer and horrifically murdered one by one...only to wake up and find themselves back at the beginning of the same evening.

reviews.author: Manuel São Bento
reviews.content:
FULL SPOILER-FREE REVIEW @ https://fandomwire.com/until-dawn-review/

"Until Dawn brings the original material to the big screen competently, especially shining in its technical aspects - mysterious atmosphere, grisly deaths, fast pacing, and an ability to keep the viewer engaged until the very end.

Ella Rubin stands out in a cast that meets the bare minimum, and David F. Sandberg proves yet again that he's a filmmaker with vision, talent, and the creativity to craft visually captivating horror sequences. Nevertheless, the flawed screenplay, lack of emotional cohesion, and a rushed ending prevent the movie from reaching a more enduring level of enjoyment.

It entertains effectively - but fleetingly."

Rating: B-

reviews.author: CinemaSerf
reviews.content: Sadly, there really isn’t much new to say about this derivative horror film. It’s the usual bunch of friends in the car routine, only this time it’s a woman-hunt they are on. You see, “Melanie” whom we very briefly meet at the start - has gone missing and so her sister “Clover” (Ella Rubin) has recruited her ex “Max” (Michael Cimino), best pal “Nina” (Odessa A’zion) and her new boyfriend “Abe” (Belmont Cameli) and the slightly spiritual “Megan” (Ji-young Yoo) to try to find out what happened. As the song goes: “if you go into the woods tonight, you’re in for a big surprise…” and so dodgy and ill-conceived decisions galore now ensue as the usual set-piece housebound horror kicks in and the story sort of lurches around like a gory version of “Groundhog Day”. The acting and writing vie for the award for being the blandest - especially the shockingly wooden Cameli, and the whole thing recycles itself to the point where I was quickly on the side of the perpetrator of these dastardly goings-on. What’s more annoying is that the plot did have some potential; it could have been better had the director relied less on the tried and tested formulae and taken a few risks with the story. As it is, his only risk was to engage a forgettable cast and leave us with an halfway house between the mystic and the makeshift. It’s an adequate summer release, but not in the least scary nor memorable.

reviews.author: MovieGuys
reviews.content:
"Until Dawn" is what I call "Scoobie Do" for adults. There's a group of pals, out for a vacation romp, who find themselves facing a mysterious back story and lots of supernatural baddies, out to croak them, in bloody style.

What makes this even worse than the usual formulaic, survivalist, horror nonsense, is its story is based upon a time loop. So, in essence, this is a horror flick, with obsessive compulsive disorder. The murder and mayhem repeats itself, stripping away even the basic sense of the unknown, as we stop wondering and worrying over, who is going to die and when. 

I can see how this would work in the context of a video game, which this film, is based upon. In games players die over and over, until they finally find a way to beat the game. As a film, its not a great idea, at all. A sense of lethargy and boredom sets in, as everyone dies over and over again. 

Without sounding too negative, there is a limited upside. The initial atmosphere of dread is well established, creature effects are reasonable, as is acting, from the cast. The deaths are varied too, so its not wholly a case of deja vu. 

In summary, a basic watch that breaks the first rule of survivalist  horror, with everyone dying, repeatedly. In turn, the sense of urgency and threat is dissipated, leading to a somewhat tedious, fundamentally repetitive, watch.

reviews.author: Horseface
reviews.content:
With twenty minutes left, I was so bored, I went to read reviews while it plays out. I already opted to go to sleep less than halfway through last night, as I realized it wasn't going to be scary at all. It's beautifuly shot, and fairly mastered, though way too dark (Hollywood doesn't know how to do HDR, so everything looks like shit from them these days), and it has that Odessa actress, that's so hot.

It's just boring, not scary, the story is poorly told, and the pacing odd and events seem jumbled. Shortly before leaving to read reviews, I was thinking, "This should've been a game. I think I'd like to play that." And now I'm told it WAS a game. So I think I'll go play that.

reviews.author: kevin2019
reviews.content: "Until Dawn" certainly doesn't inspire much confidence, especially after you find out it is based on a Playstation game. So you can automatically rule out anything even approaching the cerebral and prepare to be assailed by an assortment of cardboard cut-out characters instead. These ciphers are essentially destined to be nothing more than disposable victims and ironically enough this is precisely what they are as each one of them is brutally and systematically slain until the large hourglass in the visitor center is re-set so the carnage can begin again exactly the way it happened in the "Star Trek" episode "Day of the Dove" from the original television series. This central idea quickly runs the gamut of its limited inventiveness to be replaced by the Playstation influence which now places the attractive young cast in lots of peril and being ruthlessly pursued hither and yon by grotesque - what are they? Dead people? Well, whatever they are you can be sure they certainly aren't here to impart the secret of eternal life to our youthful heroes and heroines. This all adds up to being great fun even though the ceaseless flow of blood and gore is all too often splashing around all over the place courtesy of some incredibly impressive visual effects.

reviews.content: It is a good movie of that kind for teenage persone but for a person who wants good acting and beeing surprised during a movie is not so good. I would give it a 5/10 maybe.

aiEnrichment.summary_one_sentence: When Clover and her friends search a remote valley for her missing sister, they become trapped in a deadly time loop where a masked killer brutally murders them every night.
aiEnrichment.summary_short: A year after her sister Melanie's mysterious disappearance, Clover gathers a group of friends to search the isolated valley where she was last seen. While investigating an abandoned visitor center, the group is hunted and violently slaughtered by a terrifying masked killer. However, instead of dying permanently, they wake up unharmed at the start of the exact same evening. Forced to relive the terror repeatedly, they must uncover the secrets of the valley and break the sinister cycle before they lose their sanity.
aiEnrichment.summary_long: Haunted by the mysterious disappearance of her sister Melanie one year prior, Clover convinces her closest friends to venture into a remote, forgotten valley to look for clues. Their search leads them to an eerie, long-abandoned visitor center that holds strange remnants of the area's past. As night falls, tension turns into outright horror when a relentless, masked killer begins stalking the group through the shadowed premises. One by one, Clover and her friends suffer gruesome deaths at the hands of the murderer. Just as Clover succumbs to her fatal injuries, she suddenly snaps awake, completely unharmed, back at the start of the evening. Horrified to realize her friends are trapped in the exact same time loop, they are forced to endure the nightmarish slaughter again and again. With each reset, the group tries to alter their choices, fight back, and escape the valley, but the killer seems to anticipate their every move. To survive the repeating nightmare, Clover must piece together the connection between the killer, the valley's dark history, and her sister's disappearance.
aiEnrichment.synopsis: One year after her sister Melanie mysteriously vanished without a trace, Clover leads her friends deep into a remote and forgotten valley in search of answers. Their investigation brings them to an abandoned visitor center, but their search for closure quickly turns into a fight for survival when a violent, masked killer begins hunting them down one by one. As fear and paranoia take hold, the group faces a terrifying supernatural twist that turns their desperate night of survival into an inescapable horror.

story_structure.resolution: Clover unravels the ultimate truth behind her sister's disappearance and determines whether she and her friends can finally escape the endless night.
story_structure.introduction: One year after her sister Melanie mysteriously disappeared, Clover and her friends arrive at a remote valley to search for answers in an abandoned visitor center.
story_structure.risingAction: As Clover and her friends are killed one by one, they wake up back at the start of the evening, realizing they are trapped in a time loop; they must use each reset to piece together clues about Melanie's fate and outsmart the killer.

faq.question: What is the dominant genre of the film?

faq.answer: Yes, it is a film adaptation expanding on the universe of the popular PlayStation narrative horror video game franchise, 'Until Dawn'.
faq.question: Is this movie part of an existing franchise?

faq.answer: Yes, there is a mid/post-credits tease that shifts the focus to a snow-covered lodge, hinting at further connections to the original video game storyline and setting up potential future installments.
faq.question: Is there a post-credit scene?

faq.answer: The central premise revolves around a group of friends caught in a supernatural death loop, where they are repeatedly killed by horror monsters/killers only to reset back to the start of the night each time they die.
faq.question: What is the central premise or plot mechanism of the movie?

faq.answer: The lead protagonist is Clover, played by Ella Rubin, who travels to Glore Valley to uncover the truth about her sister Melanie's disappearance.
faq.question: Who is the main protagonist searching for her missing sister?

faq.answer: The overarching mastermind behind the psychological experiments and horrific time loop is Dr. Hill, played by Peter Stormare.
faq.question: Who is the main antagonist controlling the death loop and horrors?

faq.answer: The group faces a terrifying variety of deadly threats in each loop, including a masked slasher killer, gruesome traps, and monstrous mutated Wendigos.
faq.question: What specific threats do the characters face inside the visitor center and surrounding valley?

faq.answer: The characters have a maximum of 13 nights (or death cycles) to break free before they succumb permanently and transform into monsters.
faq.question: How many chances or nights do the characters have to escape the loop?

faq.answer: The story takes place in Glore Valley, a remote, abandoned mining town in Pennsylvania featuring an old visitor center and underground mines.
faq.question: Where does the story take place?
